output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in our own systems, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation suite, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados and kept a 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification is 4.0°C. All five Meridane containers with the Tallis-sent instructions ran at 7°C and were rejected. All four containers booked by email at 4°C passed. That includes Pellacor-treated fruit on Coastway and old-stock fruit on Meridane's K1. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. Suspending Lower Serra or reverting the fungicide would not fix the cause. Lower Serra fruit does show higher decay inside the rejected containers. That may be a secondary effect, but it is unproven. Confidence is high, about 90%. Next steps: correct the temperature in the product record today. One Meridane container is at sea and one is queued for 10 Oct, so have Meridane reset both to 4°C. Add a check of reefer settings against the product specification before each submission. Hold the claim, the suspension and any invoice deduction. Loggers are a reasonable extra control.
